purpose: In-memory key-value caching service, used to reduce database load by caching frequently-read data.
description: Memcached has no built-in authentication by default and was designed to be used only on a trusted internal network. An instance reachable from the internet allows anyone to read, write, or flush cached data, and — if UDP is enabled — can be abused as a massive DDoS amplification vector (amplification factors over 50,000x have been observed).
misconfigurations: bound to 0.0.0.0 instead of localhost/private interface
UDP protocol left enabled when only TCP is needed
no firewall rule restricting access to application servers
attack_patterns: Send crafted UDP requests to reflect and amplify traffic at a victim (DDoS amplification)
Read cached data directly with `get` commands to recover session tokens or query results
Flush or poison the cache to degrade application availability or integrity
real_world_incidents: Memcached UDP amplification was used in some of the largest recorded DDoS attacks (including a 1.3+ Tbps attack in 2018), all originating from publicly reachable memcached servers with UDP enabled.
recommended_actions: Bind memcached to localhost or a private/internal interface only — never 0.0.0.0.
Disable UDP support entirely (-U 0) unless a specific feature requires it.
Firewall the port to only the application servers that need it.
Do not cache sensitive data (session tokens, PII) without considering that the cache itself has no access control.

audience_guidance.student: Memcached is a fast temporary storage shelf for data an app doesn't want to keep re-fetching from a database. It was built for trusted internal networks only — it has no lock on the door — so exposing it to the internet lets anyone read what's on the shelf, or use it to blast huge amounts of traffic at someone else (DDoS amplification).
audience_guidance.developer: Never bind memcached to a public interface. Set `-l 127.0.0.1` (or your private subnet) and pass `-U 0` to disable UDP unless you specifically need it.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: An open memcached port is almost always an immediate high-severity finding — confirm with a raw `stats` command and check whether UDP is also open (amplification risk).
audience_guidance.pentester: Demonstrate impact by reading live cached keys, and if UDP is open, document the amplification factor as a DDoS risk in addition to the direct data-exposure risk.
audience_guidance.security_team: Any memcached instance reachable from outside the application's own VPC/subnet should be treated as a critical misconfiguration — audit firewall rules across all caching infrastructure.
